intent: Recover corrupted or missing repository files only from an authoritative, independently verifiable source; preserve file identity and bind every validation result to one immutable candidate SHA.
non_goals: Do not synthesize replacement source code when authoritative content is unavailable.
Do not strip corruption markers and call the result recovered without source comparison.
Do not weaken, skip, or relabel a failing quality gate as passing.
Do not treat a PR merge SHA, head SHA, production anchor SHA, or UI-reported SHA as interchangeable.
source_authority_rules: Prefer an exact blob at a recorded commit in the canonical source repository.
Accept a recovered-branch or forensic archive only when repository identity, commit or archive provenance, exact path, and content hash are independently recorded.
Compare Git blob SHA and a cryptographic content hash before restoring; retain the original source locator and evidence.
If the source repository, commit, path, or blob cannot be retrieved and verified, assign BLOCKED_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and leave the candidate file unchanged.
path_identity_rules: Match exact repository-relative paths; never substitute a same-named file from another directory.
Record rename or move evidence explicitly; a path collision is not proof of equivalence.
Reject empty, BOM-only, truncated, invalid-encoding, or syntax-invalid content as recovered source.
Treat UTF-8 BOM removal as normalization only after the underlying content has been proven identical to the authoritative source.
sha_binding_rules: For pull_request workflows, github.sha is the synthetic merge-candidate SHA; for workflow_dispatch, use inputs.target_sha when explicitly provided, otherwise github.sha.
Record PR head SHA and synthetic merge-candidate SHA separately; do not treat the workflow-run head_sha metadata as proof of the commit actually checked out.
Every gate must assert and log TARGET_SHA == git rev-parse HEAD and report the tested tree SHA.
M.2, CI Lite, Unified 10x10, Unified Final Gate, and Completion Validation must use the same target selection expression inputs.target_sha || github.sha.
A validation bundle is eligible for Final Gate only when all required checks name the same candidate SHA/tree or explicitly declare a separate base/head comparison.
If a workflow checks out a different SHA than the declared candidate, mark SHA_MISMATCH and do not reuse its PASS status.
Do not rewrite canonical history or silently promote the working candidate to production truth.
required_recovery_sequence: Inventory corrupted, missing, duplicate-path, renamed, and suspiciously empty files.
Trace each path through PR diff, parent commits, canonical source repository, and available forensic archives.
Capture source locator, source commit, exact path, Git blob SHA, SHA-256, target blob SHA, and comparison result.
Restore only exact, proven source content in a minimal-diff commit.
Write BLOCKED_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE to the recovery ledger for every file without verified source evidence.
Run syntax/encoding checks, path inventory, duplicate-path checks, source hash checks, targeted regression tests, and the full required CI/gate set.
Re-read the final candidate SHA and each gate's tested SHA; reject mixed-SHA evidence.
Request Final Gate only after every required check is successful on the declared candidate and no unresolved blocker remains.
